help_host: Hostname or IP address of the NUT server (e.g. 192.168.1.100)
help_port: Port the NUT server listens on — 3493 unless upsd was configured differently
help_networkInterface: Select a specific network interface for outgoing connections (optional)
help_pollInterval: How often to query the NUT server (2–300 seconds)
help_username: NUT username (optional — required for commands and writable variables)
help_password: Password of that NUT user, stored encrypted. Only needed for commands and writable variables
help_commandTimeout: Timeout for individual NUT commands (1–30 seconds)
help_enableCommands: Allow sending instant commands (INSTCMD) to the UPS — requires authentication
help_enableSetVar: Allow changing writable UPS variables (SET VAR) — requires authentication
aboutInfo: ioBroker.nut2 monitors UPS devices via the Network UPS Tools (NUT) protocol. All UPS devices connected to a NUT server are automatically discovered.
driver.name: Driver name
input.transfer.bypass.outlimits: Bypass on output out of limits
help_useTls: Encrypt the connection via STARTTLS — recommended when sending a username and password
help_tlsRejectUnauthorized: Reject self-signed or invalid certificates. Leave off for a typical self-signed NUT server; enable for man-in-the-middle protection (a CA file below lets you trust your own certificate)
help_tlsCaFile: Path to a PEM file on the ioBroker host with the certificate authority (or the self-signed server certificate) the strict check should trust — leave empty to trust the system certificate store only
descChannelDevice: Identity of the device as reported by the driver
descChannelDriver: The NUT driver talking to this UPS
descChannelInput: Mains side: what the UPS receives
descChannelOutput: Load side: what the UPS delivers
descChannelUps: The UPS itself: load, power and its own settings
descChannelAmbient: Readings of a connected environment sensor
descChannelStatus: The UPS status, split into individual flags
descChannelCommands: Buttons that send a command to the UPS
descChannelUpsInfo: How this adapter sees the UPS
descUpsReachable: The UPS answered the last poll
descUpsLastNotify: Last upsmon event routed to this UPS
descStatusRaw: The status exactly as the UPS reports it
descStatusDisplay: The same status in words, for a display or a message
descStatusSeverity: How serious the power situation is: 0 fine, 4 shutdown imminent
descFlagOnline: The UPS runs on mains power
descFlagOnBattery: Mains power is gone — the battery is carrying the load
descFlagLowBattery: The battery is nearly empty — shutdown is close
descFlagHighBattery: The battery voltage is above its normal range
descFlagReplaceBattery: The UPS asks for a new battery — it failed its own test
descFlagBypass: The load is fed straight from the mains — the UPS is not protecting it
descFlagCalibrating: The UPS is measuring its battery to re-learn the runtime
descFlagOff: The UPS output is switched off — connected devices have no power
descFlagOverloaded: More is drawn than the UPS can deliver
descFlagTrimming: Mains voltage is too high — the UPS is lowering it
descFlagBoosting: Mains voltage is too low — the UPS is raising it
descFlagForcedShutdown: Shutdown has been ordered — connected systems should power down now
descFlagAlarm: The UPS raised an alarm of its own
descFlagWaiting: The server has not heard from the driver yet
descFlagEcoMode: Energy-saving mode: the UPS filters less to waste less
descBatteryCharge: How full the battery is right now
descBatteryChargeLow: Below this level the UPS reports a low battery
descBatteryRuntime: Estimated time the battery still carries the current load
descBatteryType: Battery chemistry, e.g. PbAc for lead-acid
descBatteryChargerStatus: What the charger is doing — some UPSes report this instead of the charging flags
descDeviceType: What kind of device this is — a UPS, a power strip, a transfer switch
descDriverFlagIgnorelb: The driver ignores the UPS's own low-battery signal and uses its own threshold
descDriverParameterPollfreq: How often the driver reads the full variable set from the UPS
descDriverParameterPollinterval: How often the driver checks the UPS status — the fastest any value can change
descInputTransferHigh: Above this mains voltage the UPS switches to battery
descInputTransferLow: Below this mains voltage the UPS switches to battery
descInputVoltage: Mains voltage arriving at the UPS
descInputFrequency: Mains frequency arriving at the UPS
descInputVoltageExtended: The UPS tolerates a wider mains range before switching to battery
descOutputVoltage: Voltage the UPS delivers to the connected devices
descOutputVoltageNominal: The voltage this UPS is built for
descOutputFrequencyNominal: The frequency this UPS is built for
descUpsStatus: The raw status tokens — the parsed flags live under status
descUpsLoad: How much of the UPS capacity the connected devices use
descUpsPower: Apparent power drawn from the UPS
descUpsRealpower: Actual power drawn from the UPS — this is what the meter counts
descUpsPowerNominal: What this UPS is rated to deliver
descUpsDelayShutdown: How long the UPS waits after a shutdown command before cutting the load
descUpsDelayStart: How long the UPS waits after mains return before powering the load again
descUpsTimerShutdown: Countdown to switching the load off — empty when none is running
descUpsTimerStart: Countdown to switching the load back on — empty when none is running
descUpsBeeperStatus: Whether the UPS is allowed to beep on events
descOutletSwitchable: Whether this socket can be switched separately
descOutletStatus: Whether this socket currently supplies power
descAmbientTemperature: Room temperature at the connected sensor
descAmbientHumidity: Room humidity at the connected sensor
descCmdBeeperEnable: Let the UPS beep on events again
descCmdBeeperToggle: Switch the beeper the other way round
descCmdLoadOn: ⚠ Power the connected devices back on
descCmdLoadOff: ⚠ Cut power to the connected devices immediately
descCmdLoadOnDelay: ⚠ Power the devices back on after the configured start delay
descCmdLoadOffDelay: ⚠ Cut power to the devices after the configured shutdown delay
descCmdShutdownReturn: ⚠ Shut the load down and switch it on again when mains returns
descCmdShutdownStayoff: ⚠ Shut the load down and leave it off until switched on by hand
descCmdShutdownStop: Call off a shutdown that is counting down
descCmdShutdownReboot: ⚠ Switch the load off and on again
descCmdShutdownRebootGraceful: ⚠ Restart the load, giving connected systems time to shut down first
descCmdShutdownDefault: ⚠ Run the shutdown the UPS is configured for
descCmdTestBatteryStartDeep: Start a full battery test — this drains the battery
descCmdTestBatteryStartLow: Test the battery down to its low-battery point
descCmdTestPanelStart: Light up the front panel so you can check it
descCmdTestFailureStart: Simulate a power failure to see whether everything reacts
descCmdTestSystemStart: Run the UPS's own overall self-test
descCmdCalibrateStart: Re-learn the runtime — the UPS drains and recharges the battery for it
descCmdBypassStart: ⚠ Feed the load straight from the mains — the UPS stops protecting it
descCmdBypassStop: Put the load back behind the UPS
descCmdResetInputMinmax: Clear the recorded minimum and maximum input values
descCmdResetWatchdog: Tell the UPS the system is still alive
descConnectionStatus: The adapter is talking to the NUT server — this does not say whether the credentials are accepted
descUpsCountTotal: How many UPS devices the NUT server offers
descUpsCountReachable: How many of them answered the last poll
descUpsAllReachable: One line to watch instead of every device — false while nothing was found at all
descNotifyTrigger: Write here to poll at once — upsmon can push its events into this state
testHostRequired: Enter the NUT server host first
testConnectedNoUps: Connected %s — the server lists no UPS, so the credentials could not be checked
testConnectedAuthRejected: Connected %s, but the NUT server rejected the credentials for "%s" — reading works, switching and writing will be refused. %s UPS(es): %s
descBatteryChargeApprox: A rough estimate of the charge, not a measured value — some UPS models only report a range
descBatteryChargeRestart: The UPS only switches the load back on once the battery has reached this charge level
descBatteryChargeWarning: Charge level at which the UPS reports a warning — earlier than the low-battery threshold
descBatteryAlarmThreshold: Charge level below which the UPS raises a battery alarm
descBatteryCapacity: Nominal battery capacity in ampere-hours — how much energy the pack can store
descBatteryCapacityNominal: Capacity the battery had when new — compare it with the current capacity to judge ageing
descBatteryChargerType: Charging method the UPS uses, e.g. ABM or constant trickle charging
descBatteryCurrent: Current flowing into or out of the battery — negative while discharging
descBatteryCurrentTotal: Total current across all battery packs together
descBatteryEnergysave: Energy-saving mode: the UPS switches itself off on battery once the load is negligible
descBatteryEnergysaveDelay: How long the load must stay below the energy-saving threshold before the UPS switches off
descBatteryEnergysaveLoad: Load below which the energy-saving shutdown starts counting
descBatteryEnergysaveRealpower: Active power below which the energy-saving shutdown starts counting
descBatteryPacks: How many battery packs the UPS is fitted with
descBatteryPacksBad: How many of the battery packs the UPS considers faulty
descBatteryPacksExternal: How many of the battery packs are external add-on modules
descBatteryProtection: Deep-discharge protection — the UPS cuts off before the battery is damaged
descBatteryRuntimeLow: Remaining runtime at which the UPS reports a low battery
descBatteryRuntimeRestart: Runtime the battery must have again before the UPS switches the load back on
descBatteryDateMaintenance: When the battery is due for its next change or maintenance
descBatteryTemperatureCellMax: Highest cell temperature in the pack — a large spread points at an ageing cell
descBatteryTemperatureCellMin: Lowest cell temperature in the pack — compare it with the maximum
descBatteryVoltageCellMax: Highest cell voltage in the pack — a large spread points at an unbalanced cell
descBatteryVoltageCellMin: Lowest cell voltage in the pack — compare it with the maximum
descBatteryVoltageHigh: Voltage at which the battery counts as fully charged
descBatteryVoltageLow: Voltage at which the battery counts as empty
descBatteryVoltageNominal: Rated battery voltage — the design value, not the current reading
descDeviceMacaddr: Network address of the UPS management card
descDevicePart: Manufacturer's part number — needed when ordering a replacement
descDeviceUptime: How long the device has been running without a restart
descDeviceUsbVersion: USB protocol version the device speaks — useful when a driver misbehaves
descDeviceCount: How many devices this driver reports — more than one on a daisy chain
descDriverState: What the driver is doing right now, e.g. quiet or updating its readings
descDriverFlagAllowKillpower: ⚠ Allows the driver to cut the UPS power at the end of a shutdown — read-only here
descUpsAlarm: Plain-text alarm from the UPS — empty while there is nothing to report
descUpsContacts: State of the UPS's dry contacts, as a hexadecimal bit pattern
descUpsDelayReboot: How long the UPS stays off during a reboot before it powers the load again
descUpsDisplayLanguage: Language of the UPS's own front-panel display
descUpsEfficiency: How much of the drawn power reaches the load — the rest is lost as heat
descUpsLoadHigh: Load above which the UPS considers itself overloaded
descUpsMode: Operating mode the UPS is running in, e.g. normal, eco or high efficiency
descUpsRealpowerNominal: Active power the UPS is rated for, in watts — the limit for the load
descUpsShutdown: Whether the UPS will shut down on command — the master switch for shutdown commands
descUpsStartAuto: Whether the UPS starts the load again by itself once mains power returns
descUpsStartBattery: Whether the UPS may be switched on from battery, without mains power
descUpsStartReboot: Whether the UPS restarts the load after a shutdown instead of staying off
descUpsTestDate: When the UPS last ran a self-test
descUpsTestInterval: How often the UPS tests its battery on its own
descUpsTestResult: Outcome of the last battery self-test
descUpsTimerReboot: Countdown to the scheduled restart — empty while none is running
descUpsWatchdogStatus: Watchdog: the UPS restarts the load if the server stops reporting in
descVoltageHighCritical: Upper critical limit for the voltage — above it the device reports a fault
descVoltageHighWarning: Upper warning limit for the voltage — above it the device warns
descVoltageLowCritical: Lower critical limit for the voltage — below it the device reports a fault
descVoltageLowWarning: Lower warning limit for the voltage — below it the device warns
descVoltageMaximum: Highest voltage the device has seen since the last reset
descVoltageMinimum: Lowest voltage the device has seen since the last reset
descVoltageNominal: Rated voltage the device is designed for — not the current reading
descVoltageStatus: Whether the voltage is within its limits, or how far outside
descCurrentHighCritical: Upper critical limit for the current — above it the device reports a fault
descCurrentHighWarning: Upper warning limit for the current — above it the device warns
descCurrentLowCritical: Lower critical limit for the current — below it the device reports a fault
descCurrentLowWarning: Lower warning limit for the current — below it the device warns
descCurrentMaximum: Highest current the device has seen since the last reset
descCurrentMinimum: Lowest current the device has seen since the last reset
descCurrentPeak: Highest short current peak the device has measured
descCurrentStatus: Whether the current is within its limits, or how far outside
descInputVoltageHighCritical: Upper critical limit for the voltage — above it the device reports a fault
descInputVoltageHighWarning: Upper warning limit for the voltage — above it the device warns
descInputVoltageLowCritical: Lower critical limit for the voltage — below it the device reports a fault
descInputVoltageLowWarning: Lower warning limit for the voltage — below it the device warns
descInputVoltageMaximum: Highest voltage the device has seen since the last reset
descInputVoltageMinimum: Lowest voltage the device has seen since the last reset
descInputVoltageNominal: Rated voltage the device is designed for — not the current reading
descInputVoltageStatus: Whether the voltage is within its limits, or how far outside
descInputCurrentHighCritical: Upper critical limit for the current — above it the device reports a fault
descInputCurrentHighWarning: Upper warning limit for the current — above it the device warns
descInputCurrentLowCritical: Lower critical limit for the current — below it the device reports a fault
descInputCurrentLowWarning: Lower warning limit for the current — below it the device warns
descInputCurrentNominal: Rated current the device is designed for — not the current reading
descInputCurrentStatus: Whether the current is within its limits, or how far outside
descInputFrequencyNominal: Rated frequency the device is designed for — not the current reading
descInputFrequencyStatus: Whether the frequency is within its limits, or how far outside
descInputPhases: How many phases the mains feed has — 1 for a household socket, 3 for three-phase
descOutputPhases: How many phases the UPS delivers to the load
descInputPhaseShift: Angle between the phases — 120° is the normal value in a healthy three-phase feed
descInputQuality: How clean the incoming mains is, as the UPS judges it
descInputSensitivity: How readily the UPS switches to battery — lower sensitivity tolerates a noisier mains
descInputSource: Which supply the UPS is drawing from right now
descInputSourcePreferred: Which supply the UPS uses when it has the choice
descInputRealpower: Active power drawn from the mains, in watts
descInputRealpowerNominal: Active power the input is rated for, in watts
descInputLoad: How much of the input's rated capacity is being used
descInputPower: Apparent power drawn from the mains, in volt-amperes
descInputEcoSwitchable: Whether eco mode can be switched on for this input
descInputFeedColor: Colour code of the feed cable — helps identify it in the rack
descInputFeedDesc: Name of the feed this input is connected to
descInputFrequencyExtended: Whether the UPS accepts a wider frequency band than the standard one
descInputFrequencyHigh: Highest mains frequency the UPS still accepts before switching to battery
descInputFrequencyLow: Lowest mains frequency the UPS still accepts before switching to battery
descInputFrequencyNominalRange: How far the frequency may stray from its rated value, as a percentage
descFrequencyNominal: Rated mains frequency — 50 Hz in Europe, 60 Hz in North America
descOutputCurrent: Current the UPS is delivering to the load
descOutputCurrentNominal: Current the output is rated for — the limit for the connected load
descOutputFrequency: Frequency the UPS delivers — on battery it generates this itself
descOutputPower: Apparent power delivered to the load, in volt-amperes
descOutputInverterLatency: How long the inverter needs to take over when the mains fails
descInputBypassVoltage: Voltage on the bypass line — the path that feeds the load past the inverter
descInputBypassFrequency: Frequency on the bypass line — must match before the UPS may switch over
descInputBypassSwitchable: Whether the load can be moved to the bypass line at all
descInputBypassSwitchOn: ⚠ Moves the load onto the bypass line — it then runs unprotected on raw mains
descInputBypassSwitchOff: Takes the load off the bypass line and back onto the inverter
descInputTransferDelay: How long a mains fault must last before the UPS switches over
descInputTransferReason: Why the UPS last switched to battery
descInputTransferHysteresis: Gap between switching over and switching back, so the UPS does not oscillate
descInputTransferHighMax: Highest value the upper transfer threshold may be set to
descInputTransferHighMin: Lowest value the upper transfer threshold may be set to
descInputTransferLowMax: Highest value the lower transfer threshold may be set to
descInputTransferLowMin: Lowest value the lower transfer threshold may be set to
descInputTransferBoostHigh: Above this voltage the UPS stops boosting a low mains
descInputTransferBoostLow: Below this voltage the UPS starts boosting a low mains instead of switching to battery
descInputTransferTrimHigh: Above this voltage the UPS starts trimming a high mains instead of switching to battery
descInputTransferTrimLow: Below this voltage the UPS stops trimming a high mains
descInputTransferBypassHigh: Above this voltage the bypass line is no longer considered usable
descInputTransferBypassLow: Below this voltage the bypass line is no longer considered usable
descInputTransferBypassForced: Whether the UPS may move the load to the bypass even when conditions are poor
descInputTransferBypassOverload: Whether the UPS moves the load to the bypass when it is overloaded
descInputTransferBypassOutlimits: Whether the UPS moves the load to the bypass when its output leaves the allowed range
descInputTransferFrequencyBypassRange: How far the frequency may stray before the bypass is refused, as a percentage
descInputTransferFrequencyEcoRange: How far the frequency may stray before eco mode is left, as a percentage
descInputTransferEcoHigh: Above this voltage the UPS leaves eco mode and runs the load through the inverter
descInputTransferEcoLow: Below this voltage the UPS leaves eco mode and runs the load through the inverter
descOutletCount: How many switchable outlets this device has
descOutletId: Number of this outlet as the device counts it
descOutletDesc: Name the device carries for this outlet — often set by the user
descOutletDelayShutdown: How long the device waits before it switches this outlet off
descOutletGroupId: Number of this outlet group as the device counts it
descOutletGroupStatus: Whether this whole group of outlets is switched on
descOutletGroupType: What kind of group this is, e.g. a switchable section or a whole rack
descAmbientPresent: Whether this environment sensor is actually connected
descAmbientTemperatureStatus: Whether the measured temperature is within its limits, or how far outside
descAmbientHumidityAlarm: Whether an alarm is armed for the humidity of this sensor
descAmbientContactsStatus: State of this dry contact — open or closed, or active relative to its configuration
descPowerMaximum: Highest apparent power the device has seen since the last reset
descPowerMinimum: Lowest apparent power the device has seen since the last reset
descPowerPercent: Current apparent power as a share of the rating
descPowerMaximumPercent: Highest apparent power since the last reset, as a share of the rating
descPowerMinimumPercent: Lowest apparent power since the last reset, as a share of the rating
descInputCurrent: Current the UPS draws from the mains
descBatteryVoltage: Voltage at the battery — it drops as the battery discharges
descBatteryStatus: Health of the battery as the driver reports it — not the UPS status
descCmdOutletLoadOff: ⚠ Cut power to this outlet immediately
descCmdOutletLoadCycle: ⚠ Switch this outlet off and on again
descBatteryDate: When the battery was installed or last replaced — not when it was manufactured
descUpsDate: Date of the UPS's own clock — it can differ from the server's
descUpsTime: Time of the UPS's own clock — it can differ from the server's
descUpsType: How the manufacturer labels this UPS, e.g. offline — free text, unlike the device type
descDriverVersion: Version of the NUT release this driver was built from
descDriverVersionInternal: The driver's own version, counted apart from the NUT release
descDriverVersionData: Version of the data mapping a generic driver uses for this model
descUpsId: Name an administrator stored in the UPS itself — not the serial number
descUpsVendorid: USB vendor ID the device reports, in hexadecimal
descUpsProductid: USB product ID the device reports, in hexadecimal
